newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nampak sees earnings growth in year ahead.
newsitem.headline: Nampak sees earnings growth in year ahead.

text.p: South African packaging giant Nampak Ltd said on Thursday it expected its earnings to show further improvement in the the year ahead as a result of recent capital expenditure and productivity improvements.
The group earlier announced attributable earnings up 14.9 percent to 526.6 million rand for the year to September 30.

"The benefits that will flow from the capital expenditure of the last two years coupled with the ongoing drive to improve productivity should ensure a further satisfactory improvement in earnings in real terms (in 1997)," chairman Brian Connellan said in a statement.
But he warned growth in consumer demand is expected to remain low next year.
He added that he was pleased with the 1996 results as the year had seen a decline in consumer spending declined and margins had been placed under pressure by sharp rises in raw material input costs.
Total capital expenditure of 600 million rand was successfully commissioned during the year, bringing capital expenditure in 1996 and 1995 to more than one billion rand.
